- If we commit to a monthly token spend, how do the breakpoints (e.g., 10M / 50M / 200M tokens) map to per-token discounts?

- For premium models (chat-capable models with quality uplift), is there a multiplicative premium on top of the discounted per-token rate or a separate price ladder?
- Can unused commit credits roll over month-to-month or be applied as a credit ledger?

We want to build a procurement plan and need a worked example showing pricing for a mixed workload: ~30% embeddings (short vectors), 70% chat (multi-turn with KV cache). Also, procurement may ask for a small onboarding credit if we sign this quarter.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary and an example below; Karthik (pricing) and Jordan (solutions) are looped for any detail.

Short answers first:
- Breakpoints: we use a unified token pool for billing by default (embeddings + chat tokens count toward the same monthly committed token bucket).
- Model-class premiums: treated as a multiplier on the per-token rate for the tier you land in (not a separate ladder).
- Rollover: commit credits are consumed first; unused committed token credits expire after the monthly billing window unless you opt into a 3-month rolling-buffer (available on annual commitments).

Example (monthly committed tier = 50M tokens):
- Base on-demand rate (standard model): $0.00000X per token
- Discount at 50M tier: 20% off base -> committed rate for standard = $0.00000Y
- Premium model multiplier: +1.75x on committed per-token rate for chat-class premium models
- Embeddings: same token pool, but embeddings have shorter sequences so effective cost per API call is lower; per-token rate is the same unless you choose dedicated embedding-only pricing (we can discuss).

Quick worked example for a month with 50M committed tokens and expected usage of 80M tokens total (30M embeddings, 50M chat):
- Committed credits applied to first 50M tokens at committed rates
- Overage (30M) billed at on-demand (post-discount) rates unless we set a staged overage discount
- Because premium model multiplier only applies to tokens actually routed to premium variants, you can reduce cost by routing lower-priority traffic to standard models.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm target average monthly token burn for Q3? (ballpark is fine)
2) Would Quantum4 entertain an annual commit to get the 3-month rolling buffer (useful for seasonal variance)?

I can follow up with a spreadsheet and a couple of named scenarios. Would you prefer a short walkthrough next week?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Elena / Marissa — attaching a compact sheet that shows the tier breakpoints and several scenario rows. High-level notes from pricing: 

- Breakpoint bands we typically offer: 0-9.9M, 10M-49.9M, 50M-199.9M, 200M+ (we can set custom bands for large commits).
- Discount depth increases by band (example: 10% / 18% / 28% / 36% off base).
- Premium model multiplier (example): 1.45x for mid-tier premium, 1.75x for top-tier chat models (applies to committed or on-demand per-token rate after discount).
- Embeddings count toward the same pool by default. If you want a dedicated embedding slab (e.g., to guarantee posterior cost predictability for vector-heavy workloads), we can split with a blended discount and slightly lower multiplier.
- Rolling credits: for annual committed contracts we offer a 3-month rolling buffer; for monthly commits we do not roll.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time $10k credit tied to an annual commit >= $200k TCV.
